Sync Clock:
Indigo will update the alarm panel's time and date every night at 3am.
Custom State Icons:
Indigo client UI and Indigo Touch will show custom state image icons for alarm zones.
Zone Behaviour During Alarm
Zones always show their live open/closed state. When a zone sets off the alarm, its separate 'alarmState' becomes 'tripped', then 'memory' once the panel reports it restored, and returns to 'normal' when its partition is next armed (or with the 'Clear Alarm Memory' action). The State column, icon and 'displayState' show the combined picture. (This replaces the old 'Latch zones open while alarm is triggered' option.)
Panel Connection Loss
Mark devices unavailable after (seconds):
If no interface (IT-100 or Envisalink) has been connected for this long, every zone, keypad and zone group is shown as "unavailable" so stale states can't be mistaken for real ones. Last known states are kept. On reconnect the plugin requests a full status report from the panel and clears the marking once it has been processed. Minimum 5 seconds; brief reconnects shorter than this are ignored.
Logging
Log all zone state changes (override per-device setting):
When checked, every zone open/close is logged to the event log regardless of the per-zone 'Log Changes' checkbox in each zone device's config. Useful for diagnostics when you need a complete picture without re-ticking every device. Uncheck to honour each zone's individual setting.
Individual zone devices: Set all to log changes buttonSetAllZonesLogChanges
Set all to not log changes buttonClearAllZonesLogChanges
These buttons change the 'Log Changes' checkbox on every zone device straight away — clicking Cancel on this dialog afterwards does not undo them.
Startup / Missed Alarm Handling
If Indigo is offline (or the plugin is restarted) while the alarm trips, the plugin can miss the cmd 654 broadcast. When the plugin comes back up, the panel may replay alarm-memory broadcasts that LOOK like a fresh trip — but the alarm is already over. These settings control how that's handled.
Alert on detected historical alarm:
If checked, the plugin will fire the 'Historical Alarm Detected' trigger AND send an urgent email (using the same recipient as the regular alarm email) when it determines a trip happened while it was offline. The notification is clearly labelled as historical so you can tell it apart from a live alarm. Uncheck to suppress these notifications entirely (the trip will still be logged to the event log either way).
Startup grace period (seconds):
How long after plugin startup to treat cmd 654 broadcasts on partitions currently showing ready/disarmed as historical-alarm replays. Recommended: 120 (two minutes — covers normal panel re-broadcast windows). Set to 0 to disable historical-alarm detection entirely (every cmd 654 will be treated as a fresh live trip). Range: 0-600.
